headline: Sensex Slips into Red While Nifty Gains Ahead of Fed Call
why: Higher US Treasury yields weigh on global market sentiment.
Investor sentiment plunges to a 16-month low according to AAII survey.
IT sector drags performance ahead of crucial US Fed interest rate decision.
Concerns over potential aggressive Fed rate hikes re-emerge globally.
whatHappening: Sensex ended slightly lower while Nifty gained ground, driven by metals and FMCG.
Smallcap indices surged nearly 1.8% as metals sector rose 1.5%.
SBI reports FCNR(B) deposits could generate ₹5 trillion notional profit for banks.
Air India considers merging its budget unit to reduce operational costs.

summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed mixed as the Nifty gained while Sensex slipped into the red after volatile trading.
Metals and FMCG stocks performed strongly, helping drive a nearly 1.8% jump in smallcap indices despite IT sector drag.
Global markets remain cautious due to rising US Treasury yields and plunging US investor sentiment ahead of the Fed rate decision.
